content.title: About
content.content: Caesar salad with romaine is a classic dish composed of crisp romaine lettuce leaves, Parmesan cheese, croutons, and traditionally a dressing made from egg yolk, olive oil, anchovies, garlic, and lemon juice. In this version the dressing is omitted, allowing the natural bitterness and subtle sweetness of the lettuce to shine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The salad was created in the 1920s at the Tijuana restaurant “Caesar’s” for American diplomat Caesar Cardini.
Romaine lettuce is rich in vitamins A and K as well as folate.
Traditional Caesar dressing often contains raw eggs, so many recipes use pasteurized alternatives for safety.
Croutons add a crunchy texture and help hold a small amount of dressing when it is used.
A dressing‑free version is popular among those watching calories and wanting to highlight the vegetables’ natural flavor.

items.title: Rich in vitamins A and K
items.content: Romaine provides carotenoids and vitamin K, supporting vision, immunity, and blood clotting.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: Without dressing the salad contains about 15 kcal per 100 g, making it an excellent diet choice.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients in romaine help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Vitamin K and calcium in the leaves contribute to strong bones.

items.title: Leaf contamination
items.content: Salad greens can be contaminated with bacteria (E. coli, Salmonella); thorough washing is essential.

items.title: Parmesan allergy
items.content: People sensitive to dairy may react to the cheese.

items.title: High oxalate content
items.content: For individuals prone to kidney stones, excessive oxalates may be a concern.

items.title: Digestive discomfort in large portions
items.content: Eating a lot of raw greens can cause gas in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad cold, laying romaine leaves on a plate, sprinkling grated Parmesan and crunchy croutons on top. Optional additions include grilled chicken, shrimp, or tofu for extra protein.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep lettuce in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or container with a paper towel to absorb excess moisture. Use within 1‑2 days, as leaves become limp after that.
